q2.answer: The resume position lives in sync_state (download_last_id, download_pages_saved, pages_complete), and each page's product rows and the matching sync_state update are written in one SQLite transaction. The cursor therefore never runs ahead of the rows it describes, and a killed app re-fetches the one page that was not committed.

q3.answer: The watermark W is read before any page, and catch-up in step 4 replays every change with change_seq above W in commit order after the last page. The change_seq check on upserts and the no-op delete rule make overlap between pages and replayed changes harmless, so nothing created, changed or deleted during the download is missed. This relies on product ids never being reused, which is open question 2.

q5.answer: A forced re-download (resync, step 7) sets download_state to downloading and clears the download fields, then rebuilds a fresh product_next from a new watermark while product_live keeps serving reps untouched. The copy becomes the one the app reads only at the step 5 swap, which drops the old product_live, renames product_next to product_live and sets live_cursor, all in one transaction.

q9.answer: The client applies a received product only if no row exists for its id or the stored change_seq is lower than the incoming change's change_seq. Page items and change items both carry change_seq, so the comparison always has a stored value to check against, and an older or repeated record is skipped.

q10.answer: An incremental pull starts from live_cursor, the change_seq that product_live has been brought up to, and that position moves forward only in the same transaction that applies each batch of up to 1,000 changes. Until the first swap live_cursor is null, which means the device has no catalogue yet.

q11.answer: The document says the feed returns changes with change_seq greater than N in ascending order, up to the batch limit, including tombstones. A delete is represented as deleted true with product null, and the server's delete is a soft tombstone kept for 7 days. The plan does not say which table or index the server reads to build the feed, and that is not decided here.
